json5 delete beside and of a NaN
cases.note: The delete guard compares the parses before and after, and a `NaN` is compared by its lexeme, so it is equal to itself: deleting beside it, or deleting it, is not refused as a value having changed.

cases.id: json5 delete after a line comment leaves the rest of its line [1]
cases.note: A later entry that begins its line goes with the comma after it, not the one before: that one ends the line above, behind a `// t` comment, and the old splice took `\n  n: NaN`, joining the rest of `n`'s line, `i` with it, to the comment (docs/tasks/delete-splices-taking-other-values.md). Alone on its line, the entry takes the line and its own comment.

cases.id: json5 delete after a line comment leaves the rest of its line [2]
json5 delete key carries an owned /* */ block comment
json5 delete key from a packed single-line object (regression)
cases.note: Regression: a compact single-line object packs multiple entries onto one physical line — the *only* shape a minified/compact JSON object ever has — so `deleteKey`'s generic line-based delete (built for one-entry-per-line layout) used to delete the whole line, i.e. the sole remaining entry's deletion wiped the entire document, and a middle/first entry's deletion swallowed its neighbor too. Deleting one key from a packed object must leave its siblings untouched.

cases.id: json5 delete first key of a packed single-line object
delete key from a packed single-line object (regression)
delete last key of a pretty multi-line object (regression)
cases.note: Regression: deleting the *last* key of a one-entry-per-line (pretty) object used to leave the *predecessor's* separator comma dangling before the closing brace — the block-shaped line delete removes the last entry's own line but not the comma on the line above it. In strict JSON (no trailing comma allowed) that produced invalid output that failed to reparse; the flow-aware splice now drops the preceding comma instead.

cases.id: delete first key of a pretty multi-line object keeps indentation
delete only key of a single-entry object leaves an empty object
cases.note: Regression: deleting the *only* key of a single-entry object must leave an empty object `{}`, not delete the braces with the line. A packed single-line `{"a":1}` has the braces on the entry's own line, so the block-shaped line delete used to wipe the whole document (here: fail to reparse as strict JSON).

cases.id: insertValue refuses a key the mapping already holds, in every format
cases.note: Zig error DuplicateKey. The Zig test also checks the editor's internal `splice_rejected` flag, which a fixture cannot see.

cases.id: insertValue rolls back an insert that repeats a name, from key syntax
cases.note: Zig error DuplicateKey. The key arrives as syntax (`"s"`), so only the reparse knows its name. The Zig test passes key syntax (`insertKey`), where only the reparse knows the name; the binding inserts by name (`insertValue`), so these steps hold the same refusals through the up-front name check.
